AI Weekly Digest
October 12, 2026
A few things worth knowing this week — here's what's happening in AI, in plain English.
TL;DR — Top picks this week
Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
Sophos is using an OpenAI tool called Daybreak to investigate cyber‑threats. The AI cuts investigation time by 96% and automates about half of the security cases, which could mean faster protection and less manual work for our IT team.
Asana cuts model costs 76x in browser tests with GPT-6.1 Sol
Asana added a new AI model named GPT‑6 Astra to its Codex platform to run its browser‑based automation. The change made the system 76 times cheaper and five times faster in tests, so we could run AI tools at lower cost and get results more quickly.
How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
Oracle is using ChatGPT‑based tools called ChatGPT Work and Codex to capture specialist knowledge and turn it into quick, repeatable workflows for hiring, engineering and daily operations. This approach could help us standardize processes and finish work faster across the company.

Oracle is using ChatGPT‑based tools called ChatGPT Work and Codex to capture specialist knowledge and turn it into quick, repeatable workflows for hiring, engineering and daily operations. This approach could help us standardize processes and finish work faster across the company.
Read more →
Pollo AI turns creative ideas into campaigns with OpenAI
Pollo AI combines several OpenAI models to turn bold ideas into detailed images and short video ads automatically. Our marketing team could use this to create advertising material more quickly without needing external designers.
Read more →
LegalOn halves Codex costs while maintaining development speed
LegalOn reduced the daily cost of using Codex by 65% by matching the right AI model to each task and keeping a close eye on spending. This shows we could save on AI expenses while keeping our development speed the same.
Read more →
Disrupting AI-enabled “false front” operations
OpenAI disrupted two AI-enabled influence operations that used false-front journalists and a think tank to spread geopolitical messaging.
Read more →
Helping teens learn, plan, and shape the future of AI
College Planner is coming to ChatGPT for Teens to help students manage college applications, alongside new flashcards, quizzes, and a teen AI council.
Read more →
Radisson Hotel Group brings hotel discovery into ChatGPT
Radisson partnered with Accenture to build a ChatGPT plugin using OpenAI technology, helping travelers find, compare, and book hotels while planning their trips.
Read more →
GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
GPT‑6 is rolling out globally in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, delivering faster responses with visuals and interactive experiences you can explore and use directly.
Read more →
How Jump Trading is scaling quant research with ChatGPT
Jump Trading uses OpenAI to expand quantitative research. See how longer-running AI workflows combine multiple data sources with human review.
Read more →
Sharing AI progress in mathematics
OpenAI publishes new results on open problems in mathematics from an internal frontier model and shares Lean proof formalizations and research details on GitHub.
Read more →
Advancing computer use with Ironclad
Learn how OpenAI and Ironclad are training and evaluating AI agents on complex contracting workflows to advance computer use for professional work.
Read more →
